points.place: 弗吉尼亚州威斯特摩兰县
points.title: 童年与成长
points.description: 乔治·华盛顿出生于弗吉尼亚州威斯特摩兰县的种植园家庭，是奥古斯丁·华盛顿和玛丽·鲍尔·华盛顿的次子。他的童年主要在弗农庄园度过，接受了基本的教育，包括数学、土地测量和礼仪。11岁时父亲去世，华盛顿由同父异母的哥哥劳伦斯抚养。这段时期他培养了强烈的责任感、对土地的热爱以及作为弗吉尼亚贵族子弟的价值观，这些特质深刻影响了他后来的政治和军事生涯。
points.descriptionEn: George Washington was born in Westmoreland County, Virginia, to a plantation family. He spent his childhood primarily at Mount Vernon, receiving basic education in mathematics, surveying, and etiquette. His father died when he was 11, and he was raised by his half-brother Lawrence. During this formative period, Washington developed a strong sense of responsibility, love for the land, and values as a Virginia gentleman, which profoundly influenced his later political and military career.

points.title: 土地测量员生涯
points.description: 华盛顿开始了他的职业生涯，成为弗吉尼亚州的官方土地测量员。这项工作使他深入了解了弗吉尼亚的广阔领土，建立了广泛的人脉网络，并积累了大量财富。他测量了超过20万英亩的土地，包括许多后来属于他自己的土地。这段经历不仅锻炼了他的野外生存能力和精确性，还使他熟悉了边疆地区的地理和印第安部落情况，为他后来担任民兵指挥官和与印第安人打交道奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Washington began his career as an official surveyor for Virginia. This work allowed him to gain intimate knowledge of Virginia's vast territory, build extensive networks, and accumulate significant wealth. He surveyed over 200,000 acres of land, including many that later became his own. This experience not only honed his wilderness survival skills and precision but also familiarized him with the geography of frontier regions and Native American tribes, laying the foundation for his later role as militia commander and dealings with Native Americans.

points.title: 法国-印第安人战争
points.description: 华盛顿被任命为弗吉尼亚民兵中校，参与了法国-印第安人战争。他负责保卫弗吉尼亚西部边疆，对抗法国及其印第安盟友。1754年，他带领部队前往俄亥俄河谷，试图驱逐法国人，但在杜quesne堡垒附近战败并被俘。尽管如此，他因其勇敢和领导才能赢得了尊重。1755年，他作为布rad将军的副官参与了蒙农加赫拉战役，表现出色。这段军事经历使他积累了宝贵的战争经验，建立了与殖民地精英的联系，并培养了他对英国军事体系的认识，同时也加深了他对英国殖民政策的复杂情感。
points.descriptionEn: Washington was commissioned as a colonel in the Virginia militia and participated in the French and Indian War. He was tasked with defending Virginia's western frontier against the French and their Native American allies. In 1754, he led troops to the Ohio Valley to expel the French but was defeated and captured near Fort Duquesne. Despite this, he earned respect for his bravery and leadership. In 1755, he served as aide-de-camp to General Braddock in the Battle of the Monongahela, performing admirably. This military experience provided him with valuable war experience, connections with colonial elites, and understanding of the British military system, while also deepening his complex feelings toward British colonial policies.

points.title: 种植园主与政治家
points.description: 华盛顿回到弗农庄园，成为一名成功的种植园主，通过种植烟草和经营土地积累了大量财富。同时，他积极参与弗吉尼亚殖民地政治，成为弗吉尼亚议会议员。1769年，他领导反对《汤森法案》的抗议活动，成为殖民地反抗英国政策的领袖之一。1774年，他作为弗吉尼亚代表参加了第一届大陆会议。这一时期，华盛顿从英国忠实的殖民地官员逐渐转变为美国独立运动的坚定支持者，他的政治立场和领导才能使他成为殖民地反抗运动的核心人物。
points.descriptionEn: Washington returned to Mount Vernon, becoming a successful plantation owner who accumulated significant wealth through tobacco cultivation and land management. Simultaneously, he actively participated in Virginia colonial politics, serving as a member of the Virginia House of Burgesses. In 1769, he led protests against the Townshend Acts, emerging as a leader of colonial resistance to British policies. In 1774, he represented Virginia at the First Continental Congress. During this period, Washington evolved from a loyal British colonial official to a steadfast supporter of American independence, with his political stance and leadership abilities making him a central figure in the colonial resistance movement.

points.title: 美国独立战争
points.description: 华盛顿被任命为大陆军总司令，领导美国独立战争。面对训练有素、装备精良的英军，华盛顿采取了灵活的战略，包括著名的特伦顿战役和普林斯顿战役的突袭。他克服了严酷的冬季条件，如福吉谷的艰难时期，保持了军队的士气和凝聚力。1781年，他领导约克镇战役，与法国军队合作，迫使英军康华里将军投降， effectively ending major combat operations。华盛顿的军事才能、坚韧不拔的意志和对军队的严格纪律使他成为美国独立战争的关键人物，他的领导确保了美国的独立。
points.descriptionEn: Washington was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Continental Army, leading the American Revolutionary War. Facing the well-trained and equipped British forces, Washington adopted flexible strategies, including the famous surprise attacks at Trenton and Princeton. He endured harsh winter conditions, such as the difficult period at Valley Forge, while maintaining army morale and cohesion. In 1781, he led the Siege of Yorktown, coordinating with French forces to force British General Cornwallis to surrender, effectively ending major combat operations. Washington's military talent, unwavering will, and strict discipline made him a pivotal figure in the American Revolution, with his leadership ensuring American independence.

points.title: 美国总统任期
points.description: 华盛顿当选为美国第一任总统，连任两届。在他的领导下，建立了联邦政府的基本框架，包括内阁制度、最高法院和联邦司法系统。他签署了《司法条例》，建立了联邦法院系统。在外交政策方面，他坚持中立政策，避免了与欧洲列强的冲突，同时通过《杰伊条约》解决了与英国的贸易争端。1793年，他发布了《中立宣言》，确立了美国不介入欧洲事务的原则。华盛顿的总统任期奠定了美国政治制度的基础，他的辞职开创了和平权力交接的先例，避免了终身制的危险。
points.descriptionEn: Washington was elected as the first President of the United States, serving two terms. Under his leadership, he established the basic framework of the federal government, including the cabinet system, Supreme Court, and federal judiciary. He signed the Judiciary Act, establishing the federal court system. In foreign policy, he maintained a neutral stance, avoiding conflicts with European powers while resolving trade disputes with Britain through the Jay Treaty. In 1793, he issued the Proclamation of Neutrality, establishing the principle of non-involvement in European affairs. Washington's presidency laid the foundation for the American political system, and his resignation set the precedent for peaceful transfer of power, avoiding the dangers of lifelong rule.

supporter.zh: 华盛顿被誉为美国国父，他的领导才能和道德品质成为美国民主制度的基石。他放弃权力、回归平民生活的行为树立了共和主义的典范。在独立战争中，他克服重重困难，带领大陆军取得胜利；作为总统，他建立了联邦政府的框架，确立了三权分立的原则。华盛顿的坚韧、正直和无私使他成为美国历史上最受尊敬的人物之一，他的领导风格和道德标准影响了后世的政治家。
supporter.en: Washington is celebrated as the Father of His Country, whose leadership and moral character became the cornerstone of American democracy. His relinquishment of power and return to private life established a model for republicanism. During the Revolutionary War, he overcame tremendous difficulties to lead the Continental Army to victory; as president, he established the framework of the federal government and the principle of separation of powers. Washington's resilience, integrity, and selflessness make him one of the most revered figures in American history, with his leadership style and moral standards influencing generations of statesmen.

critic.zh: 批评者指出华盛顿作为奴隶主的双重标准，他一方面倡导自由，另一方面却拥有数百名奴隶。他在印第安人政策上也存在争议，参与了驱逐印第安人的战争。此外，华盛顿的精英主义倾向使他未能充分代表普通民众的利益，他的宪法设计更多保护了财产权而非民主原则。一些历史学家认为，他的军事独裁倾向在战争期间有所显现，且他对政治异议的压制也反映了其民主理念的局限性。
critic.en: Critics point out Washington's hypocrisy as a slaveholder who advocated for freedom while owning hundreds of enslaved people. His policies toward Native Americans are also controversial, as he participated in wars that displaced indigenous populations. Additionally, Washington's elitist tendencies meant he failed to fully represent the interests of ordinary citizens, and his constitutional design protected property rights more than democratic principles. Some historians argue that his authoritarian tendencies surfaced during the war, and his suppression of political dissent reflects limitations in his democratic ideals.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，华盛顿被复杂地塑造为一个既是神话人物又是历史真实的存在。他被视为美国民主制度的奠基人，其形象被理想化为诚实、勇敢和无私的象征。然而，现代历史研究也揭示了他作为奴隶主和参与印第安人政策的复杂历史。华盛顿的生平反映了美国建国时期的矛盾与张力，他的遗产既有民主理想的实现，也有奴隶制和扩张主义等阴暗面。在流行文化中，他的形象不断被重新诠释，反映了不同时代对美国建国神话的重新思考。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Washington is complexly portrayed as both a mythic figure and a historical reality. He is regarded as the founder of American democracy, idealized as a symbol of honesty, courage, and selflessness. However, modern historical research also reveals his complexities as a slaveholder and participant in Native American policies. Washington's life reflects the contradictions and tensions of America's founding era, with his legacy encompassing both the realization of democratic ideals and the darker aspects of slavery and expansionism. In popular culture, his image is continually reinterpreted, reflecting evolving perspectives on America's founding myths.

self.zh: 自由的基础是美德，而如果人民不能克制自己，那么他们既不配拥有自由，也无法保有自由。
self.en: Liberty, when it begins to take root, is a plant of rapid growth. The foundation of free government is virtue, and if the people had no virtue, they were unworthy of freedom and could not long retain it.

others.zh: 华盛顿将军的品格和才能使他成为这个国家最伟大的人物。他的智慧、勇气和无私使他赢得了所有人的尊敬。
others.en: General Washington's character and abilities have made him the greatest man of this country. His wisdom, courage, and selflessness have earned him the respect of all.
